raw_text:
Docs: tutorial for securing a FastAPI + OpenAI chatbot — open-source issue in patsypppe/slopaudit. Labels: documentation, help wanted, good first issue. ## Why
A second end-to-end tutorial (next to the LangChain one in #13) for the most common stack: a FastAPI endpoint that calls an LLM.

## What to do
1. Start from a small, deliberately unsafe app: request data in the system prompt, model output rendered or executed, a hardcoded key, no token cap.
2. Scan, explain each finding, fix it, rescan to clean, add the GitHub Action.
3. Run every command and paste real output.

## Where
New `docs/tutorial-fastapi.md`, linked from `docs/README.md`.

title: PostgresSaver drops config metadata and configurable keys from checkpoint metadata (googleapis/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg-python)
raw_text: PostgresSaver drops config metadata and configurable keys from checkpoint metadata — open-source issue in googleapis/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg-python. Labels: good first issue, help wanted, type: bug, priority: p2, api: cloudsql-postgres. Currently, `AsyncPostgresSaver.aput` (and `PostgresSaver.put`, which wraps it) stores `json.dumps(metadata)` as given. `InMemorySaver`, `SqliteSaver` and LangGraph's `PostgresSaver` store `get_checkpoint_metadata(config, metadata)` (`get_serializable_checkpoint_metadata` in Postgres), which adds `config["metadata"]` and the `configurable` keys (such as `user_id` or `run_id`) to the checkpoint metadata.
